newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares depressed as gloomy autumn beckons.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares depressed as gloomy autumn beckons.

text.p: Italian stocks ended nearly one percent lower on Monday as traders sold in expectation of an autumn of economic slowdown and difficulties over privatisation and budget plans for the centre-left government.
"The lira is positive, the Italian treasuries are positive and the stock market is terrible," one trader said, noting low volume on the market of around 349 billion lire.

"There's no interest in the market and there are fears about the state of the economy after GDP figures last week," he added. Gross domestic product data late last week showed the economy slowing more than forecast.
The blue chip Mib30 index closed 0.93 percent down at 14022 while the all-share Mibtel was off 0.81 percent at 9433.
Traders noted some other European markets had risen while U.S. markets were closed for Labor Day.

"I expected Italy to move in line with other Europeans today but the market seems to be gloomy over the prospects Italy offers in the coming months - like problems over privatisations," a trader said.

On individual stocks, information technology group Olivetti extend its recent roll downhill and closed three percent down at 765 lire, while de Benedetti holding CIR was 3.48 percent weaker at 774 lire.
Telecoms stocks state holding Stet and Telecom Italia Mobile suffered losses of around 1.3 percent to 4742 and 3073 lire respectively, again on general nervousness about privatisation prospects.
Banks also looked floppy, although Banca Commerciale Italiana and San Paolo were punished less than Credito Italiano and Ambroveneto, both off 1.8 percent.
Insurers also looked weak, with Generali and RAS around 1.9 percent down on ongoing rumours the next budget might include a tax on technical reserves.
